candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether DoorDash Commerce Platform and white-label delivery tools reduce restaurant fear of marketplace data leakage, or instead deepen merchant dependence on DoorDash infrastructure.
candidates.next_evidence: Review latest 10-K and quarterly shareholder letters for Commerce Platform revenue disclosure, merchant retention, marketplace take-rate direction, restaurant GOV growth, and restaurant versus non-restaurant mix.
candidates.node_relation: Controls a major restaurant delivery marketplace, consumer demand surface, membership frequency loop, delivery dispatch network, and merchant commerce tools.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Food delivery marketplace and merchant commerce platform
candidates.theme_relation: Reference leader for the channel-dependency risk restaurants face when incremental delivery demand flows through a third-party marketplace rather than first-party brand channels.
candidates.why_include: DoorDash is the clearest public benchmark for the economic power of restaurant demand aggregation and dispatch infrastructure.
candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed; included only as the context anchor against which first-party ordering, loyalty, and POS/payment rails should be compared.

candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether restaurants increasingly attach Toast online ordering, loyalty, marketing, and payment modules, raising switching costs and data centrality beyond basic POS.
candidates.next_evidence: Track gross payment volume, location growth, module attach rates, SaaS ARPU, net retention, restaurant churn, and whether commission-free first-party ordering is emphasized in filings.
candidates.node_relation: Provides restaurants with an integrated operating system spanning POS, payments, digital ordering, delivery, marketing, loyalty, payroll, and back-office workflows.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Restaurant vertical SaaS, POS, payments, online ordering, loyalty, and back-office platform
candidates.theme_relation: Potential beneficiary if restaurants prioritize first-party ordering, loyalty, and customer data ownership instead of relying solely on delivery marketplaces.
candidates.why_include: Toast is too large for the main underfollowed lane, but it is one of the purest public comparables for restaurant-owned digital demand infrastructure.
candidates.why_underfollowed: Not deeply underfollowed; however, the restaurant-specific breadth of its platform makes it a useful valuation and evidence benchmark for smaller restaurant-tech suppliers.

candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether Punchh and PAR Ordering are becoming strategic control points at enterprise restaurant chains rather than just replaceable modules.
candidates.next_evidence: Verify subscription revenue growth, ARR, net revenue retention, customer concentration, Burger King or other large-chain rollout status, Punchh transaction volume, and margin progression.
candidates.node_relation: Owns restaurant technology rails including PAR POS, Punchh loyalty/customer engagement, PAR Ordering, PAR Pay, and PAR OPS back-office data products.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Restaurant and retail software: POS, loyalty, digital ordering, delivery, payments, and back-office analytics
candidates.theme_relation: Underfollowed supplier to restaurant brands seeking to keep customer identity, loyalty behavior, and ordering data inside brand-controlled systems.
candidates.why_include: PAR maps tightly to the node because it sells the software stack that can preserve first-party customer relationships: loyalty, ordering, POS, payments, and operational analytics.
candidates.why_underfollowed: It is smaller than Toast and DoorDash, has a messier legacy hardware/software/government-services history, and may be screened out by investors looking only at obvious restaurant brands or delivery apps.

candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether Shift4 Dine/SkyTab merchant growth and restaurant payment volume are becoming large enough to create restaurant-specific operating leverage and switching costs.
candidates.next_evidence: Check latest filings and investor decks for restaurant merchant count, hospitality payment volume, SkyTab or Shift4 Dine adoption, take-rate, churn, partner integrations, and exposure to large restaurant groups.
candidates.node_relation: Provides integrated payments and commerce infrastructure across restaurants, hospitality, venues, retail, and e-commerce, including restaurant-focused systems and integrations.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Integrated payments, hospitality POS, restaurant commerce, and merchant software
candidates.theme_relation: Second-order beneficiary if restaurants consolidate payments, ordering, POS integrations, and customer transaction data with vertical payment platforms instead of pure delivery aggregators.
candidates.why_include: Shift4 is less pure than Toast or PAR but has meaningful exposure to restaurant and hospitality payments, POS integrations, and data-rich merchant workflows.
candidates.why_underfollowed: Often categorized as a generic payments processor, which may obscure its restaurant and hospitality-specific integration layer.

evidence.claim: DoorDash reports marketplaces and a Commerce Platform that includes white-label delivery fulfillment services and services that help merchants establish online ordering.
DoorDash stated that in 2026 it aims to increase merchant value through its Commerce Platform while expanding marketplace selection and membership programs.
evidence.source_title: DoorDash Releases Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2025 Financial Results

evidence.claim: Toast describes its platform as spanning POS, digital ordering and delivery, labor and workforce management, inventory and supply chain tools, marketing and loyalty, financial management, and related services.
Toast’s 2025 annual report describes online ordering and Order & Pay as products that can create synergies with marketing and loyalty.

PAR’s 2025 annual report groups subscription services into Engagement Cloud, including Punchh and PAR Ordering for loyalty, engagement, omnichannel ordering and delivery, and Operator Cloud including PAR POS, PAR Pay, and PAR OPS.
PAR Technology had a market capitalization of about $555 million as of June 10, 2026, based on the finance tool output used in this run.
evidence.source_title: Finance tool quote for PAR Technology Corp.

evidence.claim: Shift4 says its payment platform can be used across in-store, online, mobile, and tablet-based channels and verticals, and that some solutions include business intelligence and POS software.
Shift4’s May 2026 investor materials stated that Shift4 Dine merchant count was up 40% year over year and that the company continued to gain restaurant share.

Olo was a strong historical fit for white-label restaurant ordering, delivery, and guest data tools, but its common stock ceased trading and was delisted following the Thoma Bravo acquisition, so it is excluded from the US-listed candidate set.
evidence.source_title: Thoma Bravo Completes Acquisition of Olo

evidence.claim: External context on Domino’s highlights the importance of direct ordering, loyalty members, first-party customer data, and commission-free economics, supporting the node hypothesis that customer-relationship control is a restaurant chokepoint.

memory_update.text: PAR should remain a priority underfollowed candidate for restaurant first-party data infrastructure because its Punchh, PAR Ordering, PAR POS, PAR Pay, and PAR OPS assets map directly to loyalty, ordering, payments, and operational-data control.

Shift4 should remain in the second-order underfollowed lane as a restaurant/hospitality payments and POS-integration provider, but its thesis needs evidence on restaurant-specific mix and Shift4 Dine/SkyTab adoption.

DoorDash is the reference benchmark for marketplace-driven demand aggregation; Toast is the reference benchmark for restaurant-owned operating system rails; smaller candidates should be assessed against these two poles.
Olo would have been one of the cleanest public pure plays for white-label direct ordering and guest data, but it is no longer suitable for the US-listed universe after its acquisition and delisting.

Need a follow-up pass on speculative shadow names in restaurant voice ordering, AI phone agents, gift-card processors, franchise CRM, and customer-data platforms; SoundHound AI surfaced as a possible but high-attention and less pure candidate requiring stricter revenue-mix verification.

node: Delivery aggregators, direct ordering, loyalty, and first-party customer data
summary: Expanded the public-market universe for the restaurant digital-demand-control node. The cleanest reference anchor is DoorDash because it controls marketplace traffic, delivery dispatch, membership frequency, and merchant commerce tools. Toast is a large but unusually pure restaurant operating-system reference name. The underfollowed lane is better represented by PAR Technology and Shift4: both sit one step away from the consumer-facing delivery debate and monetize restaurant ordering, POS, loyalty, payments, and operational data rails. Olo would have been a strong historical candidate for white-label ordering, but it is excluded from the candidate list because external evidence indicates its common stock ceased trading after the Thoma Bravo acquisition.
